# SetupRunner

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.Setup` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Setup/SetupRunner.cs#L196)

Runs a list of [`SetupStep`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/SetupStep) one at a time, across the script reloads that setting
a project up unavoidably causes.
This is the part that used to be missing. Switching platform, adding a package and importing a
sample each recompile the project, and a recompile throws away every static field and every
subscription in the editor - which is why the old setup was split into three menu items the
user had to click in the right order. The position in the sequence lives in
[`SessionState`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/SessionState.html) instead of in a static field, so it survives a reload, and the
owner of the sequence rebuilds its step list from `[InitializeOnLoadMethod]`and hands it
back through [`Resume(string, Func<IEnumerable<SetupStep>>, Action<SetupOutcome>)`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/SetupRunner#resume-string-setupstep-setupoutcome). SessionState is deliberately not EditorPrefs: closing Unity
mid-setup should forget the sequence rather than restart it days later.
What each step is doing is written to [`Progress`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/SetupRunner#progress) as it happens, which is how a
window shows the run rather than the console being the only place to watch it.

### SetSummary(string) {#setsummary-string}

### Start(string, IEnumerable\<SetupStep>, Action\<SetupOutcome>) {#start-string-setupstep-setupoutcome}

Starts a sequence. The id only has to be stable across reloads of the same sequence, so
[`Resume(string, Func<IEnumerable<SetupStep>>, Action<SetupOutcome>)`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/SetupRunner#resume-string-setupstep-setupoutcome) can tell "my sequence is still pending" from "someone else's is".
